root_causes.description: The email service (a leaf downstream of checkout) shows container lifecycle churn with its memory working set fluctuating sharply between a ~40MB median and a ~154MB peak across the window, consistent with the container restarting in a crash loop while error/CPU metrics for its callers stay nominal. This matches the known email pod_crash pattern in which Kubernetes repeatedly restarts the failing email container.

evidence.observed_value: mean=63279104, p50=40583168, p95=154060800, p99=154095206, max=154103808 bytes — working set swings ~4x above the ~40MB median up to ~154MB
evidence.expected_baseline: stable ~40583168 bytes (p50) with low variance for a healthy idle leaf service

evidence.observed_value: max=0.000 across window (no restart delta captured in this 5m sampling window)
email error_rate=0.000 (no error propagation from the leaf)

root_causes.description: The only clearly anomalous metric in the sweep is email's container memory working set, which spikes from a ~40MB median to ~154MB. If the container is not restarting, this could instead reflect an injected memory-pressure/stress fault on the email container.

evidence.expected_baseline: memory working set stable near ~40583168 bytes (p50)
near-zero idle CPU, so memory is the dominant stress signal

root_causes.description: frontend was the only service with a non-zero (though tiny) server error rate in the sweep (mean 0.003, p95/p99 0.010), which could reflect minor propagated noise rather than a true fault origin; no CPU, memory, or restart anomaly was observed.

evidence.expected_baseline: normal frontend CPU, no resource anomaly

remediation_steps: Inspect the email pod (email-*) with kubectl describe to read the restart/back-off events and container exit codes, and confirm whether the container is in CrashLoopBackOff.
Review the email container spec/ConfigMap for a recent 'container definition changed' trigger and roll back the change that forced the container restart.
Check the email container memory limits/requests and logs for OOMKilled or unhandled-exception exits; raise limits or fix the crashing code path accordingly.
Monitor email error_rate, container_memory_working_set_bytes and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total after the fix to confirm the crash loop has cleared.
